pretreatments.description: Thermal pre-treatment (TP) was applied to food waste at five different temperatures (60, 80, 100, 120, and 140 °C) with varying treatment durations (1 hour for 60 and 80 °C; 30 minutes for 100, 120, and 140 °C). This method utilized an oven to promote hydrolysis by disintegrating and liquefying the substrate cytomembrane, which enhances methane production and reduces retention time.

Biological pre-hydrolysis (BPH) treatment involved incubating the substrate in glass vessels flushed with nitrogen at four stages: 37 °C for 20 hours, 55 °C for 20 hours, 37 °C for 20 hours, and 55 °C for 20 hours, with a total incubation time of 40 hours at moderate temperatures. This method utilized inoculum and acidogenic bacteria to cause extracellular depolymerization of macromolecules (proteins, lipids, polysaccharides) into oligomers and monomers, enhancing soluble compounds.

Mechanical pre-treatment included mixing the received food waste with a kitchen blender to reduce particle size prior to the batch experiments. This action was performed to ensure consistent substrate handling and reduce particle size, affecting properties before anaerobic digestion without affecting the chemical composition of the substrate.
